     3	This ledger maps labels of the manuscript on the second moment of the
     4	Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with Gaussian noise fractional in time
     5	to the Lean declarations in this package. Labels and TeX line numbers refer to
     6	the manuscript revision a284420, and labels are written exactly as in its
     7	LaTeX source (for example `P:clock-copy-obstruction`). The ledger was written
     8	and reviewed at the earlier revisions cf979d6, 669ccc9, ba01d98, 3920258 and
     9	975feb3. Revision a284420 makes two mathematical edits that the ledger
    10	follows. (1) In `notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` it adds Lemma
    11	`L:spatial-fourier-bound` (lines 101-164, display `E:spatial-fourier-bound`),
    12	the deterministic bound `A_sp(g) <= 2^(1+alpha) R_alpha b^(alpha/2)` that
    13	`SpatialFourierBound` already proved, and the proof of
    14	`P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (same label and statement) now derives `R_0 < inf`
    15	from it, independently of the finiteness of `S_1^pos`, which it keeps only
    16	for the score inequality. (2) In the main file, `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`
    17	replaces its smoothing and truncation sentence by the multiplier comparison
    18	`E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (a measurable multiplier `m` in `[0,1]`,
    19	nested measurable Laplace domains, positivity after time integration,
    20	scaling asserted only for the original covariance) and its proof by the
    21	corresponding argument. The other changes since 975feb3 are prose and front
    22	matter (title, abstract, preface, a theory-outlook chapter, the reader
    23	edition, Appendices F and G, the list of notation moved to the back).
    24	Every cited label exists exactly once at a284420. Three of them are new at
    25	a284420 and do not exist at 975feb3: `L:spatial-fourier-bound`,
    26	`E:spatial-fourier-bound` and `E:damped-multiplier-comparison`. Every other
    27	cited label exists exactly once, in the same file, at both revisions, and
    28	every such cited lemma, proposition, theorem, equation and section has the
    29	same statement and proof up to whitespace and braces, except
    30	`P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (proof only), `L:damped-homogeneous-norms`

  5460	(`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `a284420`, lines
  5461	528-532: `B_1` the unit ball of `R^d` and
  5462	`R_alpha = alpha pi mu(B_1)/(2 sin(pi alpha/2))`) is exactly the resolvent at
  5463	`1`, `R_Gamma(1) = int mu(dxi)/(1+norm(xi)^2)`, and hence that
  5464	`R_Gamma(q) = q^(alpha-2) R_alpha` for `q > 0`. The second identity is the
  5465	display in the proof of `L:spatial-fourier-bound`
  5466	(`notes/integrated_spatial_occupation.tex` at `a284420`, lines 149-155). That

  5471	radial integral, `pi/(2 sin(pi alpha/2))`, is not written in the TeX; it is

  6993	Defines the wave Green measures `G_s` of the main file
  6994	(`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `a284420`) and states

  6998	lines 4128 and 7642); `d = 2, 3`, the proof of `L:higher-riesz` (lines
  6999	5179-5187), which quotes Chen (2.5), p. 7:
  7000	`G_h^(2)(dy) = 1_{|y|<h} dy / (2 pi sqrt(h^2 - |y|^2))` and
  7001	`G_h^(3)(dy) = sigma_h(dy)/(4 pi h)`, `sigma_h` the surface measure of the
  7002	radius-`h` sphere, and states "Both have mass `h` and satisfy
  7003	`G_h(hA) = hG_1(A)`" (lines 5186-5187). The list of notation
  7004	(`notes/index/list-of-notation.tex`, line 102) describes `G_t` as the "Wave
  7005	Green measure, with mass `t` and support in the closed radius-`t` ball". The
  7006	mass identity `G_s(R^d) = s` is the step of the proof of
  7007	`L:damped-homogeneous-norms` at line 881, which `DampedNormsHomog` took as
  7008	the supplied input `GreenMass G`.
  7009

   140	/-! ### Lower bounds of `E:damped-multiplier-comparison` -/
   141	
   142	/-- The first lower bound of `E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (main TeX line
   143	838, proof line 913), for any measure (in particular `mμ`): `0 ≤ N_{1,S}(θ)`
   144	for every set `S` and `a > 0`, since the integrand `λ^{a-1} R(θ+λ)` is
   145	nonnegative on `(0,∞)`. -/
   146	theorem N1on_nonneg (a θ : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (μ : Measure (Rd d)) (ha : 0 < a) :
   147	    0 ≤ N1on a θ S μ := by
   148	  have := Real.Gamma_pos_of_pos ha
   149	  unfold N1on
   150	  refine mul_nonneg (by positivity) (integral_nonneg_of_ae ?_)
   151	  filter_upwards [ae_restrict_of_ae ae_L0_pos] with l hl
   152	  exact mul_nonneg (Real.rpow_nonneg hl.le _) (resolvent_nonneg _ _)
   153	
   154	/-- The second lower bound of `E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (main TeX line
   155	839, proof lines 900-911), for any s-finite measure (in particular `mμ`) with
   156	`∫(1+|ξ|²)⁻¹ dμ < ∞` and `μ{0} = 0`, `0 < a < 1`, `θ > 0`, `S` measurable:
   157	`0 ≤ N_{2,S}(θ)²`, since `N_{2,S}(θ)² = ∫_{S ∩ (0,∞)} w_θ` (`N2onSq_eq`) and
   158	`w_θ ≥ 0`. -/
   159	theorem N2onSq_nonneg (μ : Measure (Rd d)) [SFinite μ]
   160	    (hR : Integrable (fun ξ : Rd d => 1 / (1 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) μ) (hμ0 : μ {0} = 0)
   161	    (a θ : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (ha0 : 0 < a) (ha1 : a < 1) (hθ : 0 < θ) (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
   162	    0 ≤ N2onSq a θ S μ := by
   163	  rw [(N2onSq_eq μ hR hμ0 a θ S ha0 ha1 hθ hS).2.2]
   164	  refine integral_nonneg_of_ae ?_
   165	  filter_upwards [ae_restrict_of_ae ae_L0_pos] with l hl
   166	  exact weight_nonneg μ hR a θ l ha0 hθ hl
   167	
   168	/-- `E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (main TeX lines 836-841, proof 894-913)
   169	in full, both lower and upper bounds, for a general measure: `μ` s-finite with
   170	`∫(1+|ξ|²)⁻¹ dμ < ∞` and `μ{0} = 0`, `0 < a < 1`, `θ > 0`, the integrand of
   171	`N₁(θ)` for `μ` integrable on `(0,∞)`, `g` measurable with values in `[0,1]`,
   172	`S ⊆ S'` measurable.  Conclusions: the integrand of `N_{1,g,S}` is integrable,
   173	`0 ≤ N_{1,g,S}(θ) ≤ N_{1,1,S'}(θ)`; the outer integrands of `N_{2,g,S}` and
   174	`N_{2,1,S'}` are integrable and `0 ≤ N_{2,g,S}(θ)² ≤ N_{2,1,S'}(θ)²`. -/
   175	theorem damped_multiplier_comparison (μ : Measure (Rd d)) [SFinite μ]
   176	    (hR : Integrable (fun ξ : Rd d => 1 / (1 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) μ) (hμ0 : μ {0} = 0)
   177	    (a θ : ℝ) (ha0 : 0 < a) (ha1 : a < 1) (hθ : 0 < θ)
   178	    (hN : Integrable (fun l : ℝ => l ^ (a - 1) * resolvent μ (θ + l)) L0)
   179	    (g : Rd d → ℝ≥0) (hg : Measurable g) (hg1 : ∀ ξ, g ξ ≤ 1) (S S' : Set ℝ)
   180	    (hS : MeasurableSet S) (hS' : MeasurableSet S') (hSS : S ⊆ S') :
   181	    Integrable (fun l : ℝ => l ^ (a - 1) * resolvent (smoothed μ g) (θ + l)) L0 ∧
   182	      0 ≤ N1on a θ S (smoothed μ g) ∧ N1on a θ S (smoothed μ g) ≤ N1on a θ S' μ ∧
   183	      Integrable (N2onOuter a θ S (smoothed μ g)) P2 ∧ Integrable (N2onOuter a θ S' μ) P2 ∧
   184	      0 ≤ N2onSq a θ S (smoothed μ g) ∧ N2onSq a θ S (smoothed μ g) ≤ N2onSq a θ S' μ := by
   185	  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := N1on_smoothed_mono μ hR a θ ha0 hθ hN g hg hg1 S S' hSS
   186	  obtain ⟨h3, h4, h5⟩ := N2onSq_smoothed_mono μ hR hμ0 a θ ha0 ha1 hθ g hg hg1 S S' hS hS' hSS
   187	  exact ⟨h1, N1on_nonneg a θ S _ ha0, h2, h3, h4,
   188	    N2onSq_nonneg _ (smoothed_hR μ g hg hg1 hR) (smoothed_zero μ g hμ0) a θ S ha0 ha1 hθ hS,
   189	    h5⟩

   193	/-- The multiplier class of `E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (TeX lines
   194	826-829): `g : ℝ^d → ℝ≥0` measurable with values in `[0,1]`. -/
   195	def IsMultiplier (g : Rd d → ℝ≥0) : Prop := Measurable g ∧ ∀ ξ, g ξ ≤ 1
   196	
   197	/-- The class is closed under pointwise products (TeX lines 845-846 and
   198	915-916: "products of multipliers in `[0,1]` depending only on `ξ`"). -/
   199	theorem IsMultiplier.mul {g h : Rd d → ℝ≥0} (hg : IsMultiplier g) (hh : IsMultiplier h) :
   200	    IsMultiplier (g * h) :=
   201	  ⟨hg.1.mul hh.1, fun ξ => by
   202	    simpa using mul_le_one' (hg.2 ξ) (hh.2 ξ)⟩
   203	
   204	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route (no manuscript step).  Multiplying the
   205	spectral measure by `g` and then by `h` (both measurable) is multiplying it by
   206	`g h`: `h(gμ) = (gh)μ`. -/
   207	theorem smoothed_smoothed (μ : Measure (Rd d)) {g h : Rd d → ℝ≥0} (hg : Measurable g)
   208	    (hh : Measurable h) : smoothed (smoothed μ g) h = smoothed μ (g * h) := by
   209	  unfold smoothed
   210	  rw [← withDensity_mul μ hg.coe_nnreal_ennreal hh.coe_nnreal_ennreal]
   211	  congr 1

   213	/-- The Gaussian multiplier `ξ ↦ e^{-η|ξ|²}`, as a function with values in
   214	`ℝ≥0`. -/
   215	def gaussMult (η : ℝ) (ξ : Rd d) : ℝ≥0 := ⟨Real.exp (-(η * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)), (Real.exp_pos _).le⟩

    30	/-- Euclidean space `ℝ^d`. -/
    31	abbrev Rd (d : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
    32	
    33	/-- A tempered measure: `∫ (1 + ‖x‖)^(-k) dν < ∞` for some natural `k`. -/
    34	def IsTempered {d : ℕ} (ν : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    35	  ∃ k : ℕ, ∫⁻ x, ENNReal.ofReal ((1 + ‖x‖) ^ (-(k : ℝ))) ∂ν < ⊤
    36	
    37	/-- An even measure: invariant under `x ↦ -x`. -/
    38	def IsEven {d : ℕ} (ν : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    39	  ν.map (fun x => -x) = ν
    40	
    41	/-- Positive-definiteness of `Γ` as a tempered distribution:
    42	`⟨Γ, φ ⋆ φ̃⟩` is a nonnegative real for every Schwartz `φ`, where
    43	`(φ ⋆ φ̃)(x) = ∫ φ(x + y) conj(φ(y)) dy` and `φ̃(x) = conj(φ(-x))`. -/
    44	def IsPosDefDistr {d : ℕ} (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    45	  ∀ φ : SchwartzMap (Rd d) ℂ,
    46	    (∫ x, (∫ y, φ (x + y) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (φ y)) ∂Γ).im = 0 ∧
    47	      0 ≤ (∫ x, (∫ y, φ (x + y) * (starRingEnd ℂ) (φ y)) ∂Γ).re
    48	
    49	/-- `μ` is the spectral measure of `Γ` in the manuscript's convention
    50	`Γ = ∫ e^{i ξ·x} μ(dξ)` in the sense of tempered distributions:
    51	`∫ φ dΓ = ∫ (∫ φ(x) e^{i ξ·x} dx) μ(dξ)` for every Schwartz `φ`. -/
    52	def IsSpectralMeasure {d : ℕ} (Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)) : Prop :=
    53	  ∀ φ : SchwartzMap (Rd d) ℂ,
    54	    ∫ x, φ x ∂Γ =
    55	      ∫ ξ, (∫ x, φ x * Complex.exp (Complex.I * (inner ℝ ξ x : ℝ))) ∂μ
    56	
    57	/-- Hypothesis `H:homog`. Let `d ∈ {1,2,3}` and `0 < α₀ < 1`. The spatial
    58	covariance is a nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure
    59	`Γ` on `ℝ^d` with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure `μ`,
    60	`Γ = ∫ e^{i ξ·x} μ(dξ)`; for every Borel set `A` and `c > 0`,
    61	`Γ(cA) = c^{d-α} Γ(A)`; `α₀ + α < 2` (`E:threshold`), with `0 < α < d` or
    62	`α = d = 1`. A Lean measure is nonnegative, and on `ℝ^d` a locally finite
    63	Borel measure is a Radon measure. -/
    64	structure HomogCovariance (d : ℕ) (alpha alpha0 : ℝ) (Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)) :
    65	    Prop where
    66	  dim : d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3
    67	  alpha0_pos : 0 < alpha0
    68	  alpha0_lt_one : alpha0 < 1
    69	  Γ_radon : IsLocallyFiniteMeasure Γ
    70	  Γ_even : IsEven Γ
    71	  Γ_tempered : IsTempered Γ
    72	  Γ_posdef : IsPosDefDistr Γ
    73	  μ_radon : IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ
    74	  μ_even : IsEven μ
    75	  μ_tempered : IsTempered μ
    76	  spectral : IsSpectralMeasure Γ μ
    77	  scaling : ∀ A : Set (Rd d), MeasurableSet A → ∀ c : ℝ, 0 < c →
    78	    Γ (c • A) = ENNReal.ofReal (c ^ ((d : ℝ) - alpha)) * Γ A
    79	  threshold : alpha0 + alpha < 2
    80	  alpha_range : (0 < alpha ∧ alpha < d) ∨ (alpha = d ∧ d = 1)
    81	
    82	/-- The numerical part of `H:homog`, in the form used by `DriverParameters`
    83	(with `a = α₀`). -/
    84	theorem homog_params {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
    85	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :
    86	    DriverParameters.Homog d alpha alpha0 :=
    87	  ⟨h.dim, h.alpha0_pos, h.alpha0_lt_one, by linarith [h.threshold], h.alpha_range⟩
    88	
    89	/-- `E:kappa` with the manuscript's hypothesis: under `H:homog`,
    90	`κ = (4 - α - α₀)/(3 - α) ∈ (1, 2)`. -/
    91	theorem kappa_mem_Ioo_paper {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
    92	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :
    93	    KappaRange.kappa alpha alpha0 ∈ Set.Ioo 1 2 :=
    94	  KappaRange.kappa_mem_Ioo d alpha alpha0 h.dim h.alpha0_pos h.alpha0_lt_one
    95	    h.threshold h.alpha_range
    96	
    97	/-- `E:driver-parameters` with the manuscript's hypothesis (the section
    98	retains `H:homog` and sets `a = α₀`): its strict intervals are nonempty. -/
    99	theorem parameters_nonempty_paper {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)}
   100	    (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) :
   101	    ∃ γ θ β : ℝ, (0 < γ ∧ γ < min (1 / 2) ((2 - alpha) / 2)) ∧
   102	      (1 / 2 < θ ∧ θ < β ∧ β < min (1 - alpha0 / 2) ((3 - alpha0 - alpha) / 2)) :=
   103	  DriverParameters.parameters_nonempty d alpha alpha0 (homog_params h)
   104

   803	\begin{lemma}[Homogeneous damped norms and temporal tails]
   804	  \label{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}

   101	\begin{lemma}[Deterministic Fourier bound for the spatial energy]
   102	  \label{L:spatial-fourier-bound}
   103	  Under Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, allowing $\Gamma=0$, let
   104	  $g\in C_c^\infty(\R^d;\R)$ satisfy $\|g\|_2=1$ and put
   105	  $b=\|\nabla g\|_2^2$. Then $b>0$ and
   106	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-fourier-bound}
   107	    0\le A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)
   108	    \le 2^{1+\alpha}R_\alpha b^{\alpha/2},
   109	  \end{equation}
   110	  where $R_\alpha$ is defined in~\eqref{E:intro-spectral-mass}.
   111	\end{lemma}
   112	
   113	\begin{proof}
   114	  If $b=0$, smoothness makes $\nabla g=0$ everywhere. Thus, $g$ is constant,
   115	  and compact support forces $g=0$, contrary to $\|g\|_2=1$. Put $Q=g^2$ and
   116	  use the unnormalized Fourier transform
   117	  \[
   118	    \mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)=\int_{\R^d}e^{-i\xi\cdot x}Q(x)\ud x.
   119	  \]
   120	  In the unitary convention of Section~\ref{S:masked-covariance}, this is
   121	  $c_d^{-1}\widehat Q$, with $c_d=(2\pi)^{-d/2}$.
   122	  The autocorrelation
   123	  \[
   124	    c_Q(y)=\int_{\R^d}Q(x)Q(x-y)\ud x
   125	  \]
   126	  is smooth and compactly supported. Apply the distributional spectral
   127	  identity~\eqref{E:masked-spectral-convention} to this Schwartz function.
   128	  Its inner Fourier integral is $|\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|^2$, since $Q$ is real.
   129	  Hence
   130	  \[
   131	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)=\int c_Q(y)\Gamma(\ud y)
   132	    =\int|\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|^2\mu(\ud\xi).
   133	  \]
   134	  Both integrals are finite: $c_Q$ is compactly supported and $\Gamma$ is
   135	  Radon, while $|\mathcal{F}_0Q|^2$ is Schwartz and $\mu$ is tempered.
   136	  No density of either measure is required.
   137	
   138	  Since $\|Q\|_1=1$, we have $|\mathcal{F}_0Q|\le1$. Integration by parts
   139	  and the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality give
   140	  \[
   141	    |\xi|\,|\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|
   142	    \le\|\nabla Q\|_1
   143	    \le2\|g\|_2\|\nabla g\|_2=2\sqrt b.
   144	  \]
   145	  Splitting into $|\xi|^2\le4b$ and $|\xi|^2>4b$ therefore yields
   146	  \[
   147	    |\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|^2\le\frac{8b}{4b+|\xi|^2}.
   148	  \]
   149	  The deterministic resolvent calculation in the proof of
   150	  Lemma~\ref{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}, together
   151	  with~\eqref{E:intro-spectral-mass}, gives, for $q>0$,
   152	  \[
   153	    \mathcal{R}_\Gamma(q):=\int\frac{\mu(\ud\xi)}{q^2+|\xi|^2}
   154	    =q^{\alpha-2}R_\alpha<\infty.
   155	  \]
   156	  Consequently,
   157	  \[
   158	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)\le8b\mathcal{R}_\Gamma(2\sqrt b)
   159	    =2^{1+\alpha}R_\alpha b^{\alpha/2}.
   160	  \]
   161	  Nonnegativity follows from the spectral identity. If $\Gamma=0$, then
   162	  $\mu=0$ and both sides of~\eqref{E:spatial-fourier-bound} vanish. This proves
   163	  Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-fourier-bound}.
   164	\end{proof}

1	# Stratonovich HAM second moment: Lean companion
     2	
     3	Lean 4 checks of finite, algebraic and scalar steps in the paper
     4	
     5	> Le Chen, *The second moment of the hyperbolic Anderson model* (in
     6	> preparation).
     7	
     8	The paper studies the Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model with temporal
     9	covariance `|s-t|^(-α₀)` and homogeneous spatial covariance of order `α`.
    10	It shows that `log E[u(t,x)²]` grows on the scale `t^κ`, with
    11	`κ = (4-α-α₀)/(3-α)`, and identifies the limit by a variational formula.
    12	
    13	**This is a partial formalization.** Lean checks the steps listed below. It
    14	does not check the paper end to end. The SPDE, its solution, the
    15	Stratonovich integrals, the Gaussian noise and the analytic estimates are
    16	outside Lean. Where a checked step needs such a fact, the Lean statement takes
    17	it as an explicit hypothesis, and the paper's proof supplies it.
    18	
    19	## What is checked
    20	
    21	23 modules in `StratonovichHAMAudit/`, each one step of the paper's proofs,
    22	and 66 modules in `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/` that prove the full
    23	conclusions of forty-eight labelled results and parts of further ones
    24	(ten of them are foundations: a wave-kernel and time-fractional covariance
    25	slice, finite Gaussian integration by parts, a Gaussian Schwartz test, a
    26	variational floor with weak gradients of test functions, elementary series
    27	bounds, the density of test functions in the weak-gradient `H^1`, and the
    28	finite Wick (Isserlis) formula for centered Gaussian vectors).
    29	
    30	- **With the paper's own hypotheses, nothing supplied** (most via
    31	  exact-hypothesis `_paper` wrapper theorems):
    32	  - `L:gaussian-scalar-powers` (weighted AM-GM, finite Hölder,
    33	    `E Z^r <= (E Z)^r`);
    34	  - `L:gram-scalar-algebra`;
    35	  - `L:tube-rayleigh-tail` (a Gaussian tail integral bound; its "In
    36	    particular" application excepted);
    37	  - `L:equilibrium-gamma-beta` (Gamma and Beta identities);
    38	  - `L:temporal-equilibrium` (the equilibrium density of the temporal
    39	    kernel, its potential identity on `[0,1]` and its mass);
    40	  - `L:gaussian-trace-bounds`, `P:finite-gaussian-matrix` and
    41	    `R:gaussian-one-variance-test` (moments of finite Gaussian matrix
    42	    series; the finite part of the compact Gaussian section);
    43	  - `E:kappa` (`1 < κ < 2`) and `E:driver-parameters`, under Hypothesis
    44	    `H:homog` modelled in full in Lean (covariance and spectral measures,
    45	    positive-definiteness, scaling).
    46	  - `L:variational-control-dilation` (the dilation of controls and the
    47	    scaling of mean, cost and rate), for the cost in its integral form and
    48	    the rate defined by its Rayleigh characterization; their identification
    49	    with the expectation and the spectral bottom is not formalized.
    50	  - `L:variational-heat-envelope` (the Gaussian envelope of the covariance)
    51	    and `L:variational-global-mean` (bounds and time-Lipschitz bound of the
    52	    original mean; the bounds on every mixed derivative are not
    53	    formalized).
    54	  - `P:masked-spectral-growth` (the translated spectral mass and the ball
    55	    bound); the homogeneity of the spectral measure is derived from
    56	    `H:homog`.
    57	  - `P:masked-auxiliary-norm` (the auxiliary measure `nu_R` is even,
    58	    tempered and Radon with ball bounds uniform in `R`, and the
    59	    Hilbert-valued Fourier bound `E:masked-hilbert-fourier`, proved for any
    60	    complex Banach space; the clause for a real `H` after complexification
    61	    is not formalized).
    62	  - `P:clock-copy-obstruction` (analytic clocks cannot copy the cross-pair
    63	    time transform: `0 < J <= J_1 < K`, and `J_1 = (2 - 2^a) K` when
    64	    `alpha = 1`).
    65	  - `L:masked-time-completion` (the temporal completion `H_a`, built as the
    66	    completion of `L^2(0,T)`: positive semidefinite, separable, the Schur
    67	    bound `E:masked-time-schur`, the continuous extension, the complexified
    68	    norm, interval amplitudes, and density of the real compact smooth
    69	    tests), and `L:masked-temporal-modulation` (the modulation bound);
    70	  - `L:masked-trig-products` and `L:masked-continuous-wave` (the
    71	    trigonometric products and the continuous sine factors `c_r, b_r`,
    72	    `||1_I F_r G_rho||_a^2 <= C_1(a)(1+T)^4 h^(2-a) Q_h(r,rho)` with the
    73	    paper's `C_1`, in that `H_a`).
    74	  - `P:frequency-row` and `C:frequency-time` (the uniform scalar row
    75	    `sup_xi J_h(xi) <= K C B_alpha(h)` with `K` chosen before
    76	    `d, nu, C, h`, and its time exponent above one half).
    77	  - `L:occupation-kernel-row` (the damped occupation kernel and its exact
    78	    row maximum `R_star`) and `L:spatial-physical-pair` (the physical pair
    79	    measure is sigma-finite and the pairing does not depend on the
    80	    representatives).
    81	  - `L:phase-bessel` (the Hilbert-valued finite Bessel inequality and its
    82	    conjugated version; proved for any measure space and any complete
    83	    complex inner product space, without a basis).
    84	  - `L:damped-homogeneous-norms` (the damped norms: finiteness, scaling
    85	    `N_0 = theta^(-2)`, `N_1`, `N_2^2`, temporal tails, and the
    86	    multiplier comparison `E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (both bounds, for
    87	    a general measurable multiplier in `[0,1]` and Laplace domains, and the
    88	    remarks on Gaussian smoothing in a narrower form: the Gaussian
    89	    multipliers belong to the class, without the spectral identification of
    90	    the smoothed covariance; the `N_0` mass identity; Green smoothing as a
    91	    Fourier multiplier, identified with the damped norm only in `d = 1`);
    92	    the wave Green measures `G_s`, `d = 1, 2, 3`, are built
    93	    with mass `s`, support in the closed `s`-ball and scaling
    94	    `G_s(sA) = sG_1(A)`; in `d = 3` Mathlib's sphere measure is taken as
    95	    the surface measure).
    96	  - `P:masked-quotient-obstruction` (a physical mask need not preserve
    97	    noise-null tests: for `Gamma = delta_0(dx_1) dx_2`, which Lean proves
    98	    satisfies `H:homog` with `alpha = 1`, a smooth compact mask `zeta` and
    99	    a test `F` with `E W(F)^2 = 0 < E W(zeta F)^2`; `E W(F)^2` is read as
   100	    the covariance functional of `E:cov`, the noise is not constructed).
   101	  - `P:variational-unmasked-rate` (its Rayleigh-form part: a uniform
   102	    positive floor, the Lipschitz bounds and `0 < I_Psi < infinity`; the
   103	    operator statements, including `lambda = sqrt(-E_s)`, are not
   104	    formalized).
   105	  - `L:spatial-static-controls` (the smooth temporal controls:
   106	    `lambda_z(c)^2` finite and positive, `lambda_z` Lipschitz on positive
   107	    intervals, the static score bound) and
   108	    `P:spatial-smooth-ratio` (`R_0` positive and finite, by the
   109	    deterministic Fourier bound `L:spatial-fourier-bound`, as in the
   110	    manuscript, without `T:full-upper`, and the smooth score bound); both
   111	    score bounds in an existential form and as bounds on the supremum
   112	    `S_1^pos`, whose finiteness is proved (`P:variational-positive-scores`
   113	    below).
   114	  - `L:spatial-fourier-bound` (`b > 0` and
   115	    `0 <= A_sp(g) <= 2^(1+alpha) R b^(alpha/2)` for every covariance of
   116	    `H:homog`, including zero and singular ones; with the manuscript's
   117	    constant `R_alpha`, proved equal to the resolvent
   118	    `int mu(dxi)/(1+|xi|^2)`).
   119	  - `L:positive-series-type` (the type of a positive coefficient series:
   120	    `tau = nu K^(1/nu)` in both directions).
   121	  - `C:white-relative-width` (the relative width of the white-noise bound
   122	    formulas `K_0(a)` and `M_a`; the bounds on `C_2` themselves,
   123	    `T:white-moment-bounds`, stay outside Lean) and `L:white-clock-laplace`
   124	    (the cross-pair and self-pair Laplace transforms of the white-space
   125	    falsification case, with the side condition `eta_1, eta_2 > 0` made
   126	    explicit).
   127	  - `L:inventory-product` (the coefficient bound `C^k/(k!)^nu` for the
   128	    interval inventory product, with an explicit constant `C` depending
   129	    only on `alpha, alpha0`).
   130	  - `P:spatial-four-linear` (the physical four-linear extension on `H^1`:
   131	    `A_sp(f) <= R_0 N(f)^4`, the square Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, absolute
   132	    convergence and `E:spatial-four-linear`, multilinearity and joint
   133	    continuity of `C_4` in sequential form, `R_sp = R_0` and `A_sp > 0`)
   134	    and `P:spatial-energy-map` (`E_sp = (2-alpha)/2 alpha^(alpha/(2-alpha))
   135	    R_sp^(2/(2-alpha))` in `(0, infinity)`; the static energy score bound
   136	    in an existential form and as a bound on `S_1^pos`);
   137	    the density of test functions in `H^1` that both proofs use is proved
   138	    (`H1Density`).
   139	  - `P:occupation-physical-class` (the full physical occupation class: the
   140	    pairings `B_Gamma(g_s^2, g_t^2)` are a.e.-measurable and do not depend
   141	    on the representatives, `J(g) <= R_star R_sp T(g)^(alpha/2) < infinity`,
   142	    and `0 < E_star^O <= R_star^(2/(2-alpha)) E_sp`; the class `O` is
   143	    modelled by jointly measurable representatives of `g` and `grad g`
   144	        instead of strongly `H^1`-measurable fields).
   145	  - `P:variational-positive-scores` (everything except `Q_2 >= S_2^pos`:
   146	    the value sets are nonempty and bounded above, `S_c^pos` is finite,
   147	    positive and equal to `c^((4-alpha)/(3-alpha)) S_1^pos`; the boundedness
   148	    is proved deterministically from the occupation ceiling, not by the
   149	    manuscript's stochastic argument).
   150	  - `T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling` (`c I_Psi - v_Psi/2 <= U_c` and
   151	    `S_c^pos <= U_c` for every `c > 0`, with the constant `K_0 R_sp`, an
   152	    upper bound of `C_occ`, in place of `C_occ`; the class `O`, `C_occ`, the
   153	    second form of the ceiling and `C_2 <= U_2` are not formalized) and
   154	    `C:intrinsic-spatial-bracket` (the bracket and the strict comparison for
   155	    the variational value `S_2^pos` in place of `C_2`).
   156	  - `L:positive-raw-embedding` (the variance identity in integral form, the
   157	    row bound `int_I |s-t|^(-a) dt <= K_0` and the scalar Schur bound; the
   158	    Hilbert spaces `H_t`, `H_I` are not built). The integral identities used
   159	    by `L:occupation-raw-square` are proved for continuous compactly
   160	    supported fields, a class different from the lemma's, and are not
   161	    counted.
   162	- **Every conclusion proved, with analytic inputs supplied** as named
   163	  hypotheses:
   164	  - `P:radius-mean-anchor` (the moment bound of the operator paths is
   165	    supplied);
   166	  - `L:raw-block-indexed-cone` (the cone induction behind the block
   167	    lower bound; the ground family of the compact mean family is
   168	    supplied);
   169	  - `P:moment-growth-logconvex` (log-convexity and continuity of the upper

   171	    `C:static-moment-constant-continuity` (recovery of the static moment

   184	  116|   use the unnormalized Fourier transform

    30	\begin{lemma}[Free wave form and compact Young baseline]
    31	  \label{L:symplectic-free}
    32	  There is a bounded isometric skew-adjoint $J_E$ on $E$, with $J_E^2 = -I$,
    33	  such that
    34	  \[
    35	    \omega(z,w)=\langle z,J_Ew\rangle_E
    36	    =\langle u,g\rangle_{H^{1/2},H^{-1/2}}
    37	    -\langle f,v\rangle_{H^{1/2},H^{-1/2}},
    38	    \quad z=(u,v),\quad w=(f,g).
    39	  \]
    40	  The free group preserves $\omega$. For bounded real smooth $b$, the force
    41	  $B(b)(u,v) = (0,bu)$ obeys $\omega(B(b)z,w)+\omega(z,B(b)w) = 0$.
    42	
    43	  Let $1/2 < \theta < 1$ and let $X \in C^\theta([0,T];\mathcal{K}(E))$ start at
    44	  zero, with $U_X$ its left Young evolution. Then
    45	  \begin{equation}\label{E:symplectic-compact-young-baseline}
    46	    U_X(t,s)-I\in\mathcal{K}(E),\qquad
    47	    \|S_E(t)U_X(t,s)S_E(-s)\|
    48	    \ge\|S_E(t-s)\|\ge1,\qquad 0\le s\le t\le T .
    49	  \end{equation}
    50	  More generally, for finitely many such paths $X_j$ starting at zero on $[0,B]$
    51	  and lengths $0 \le \ell_j \le B$, put $P_j = S_E(\ell_j)U_{X_j}(\ell_j,0)$.
    52	  Then
    53	  \begin{equation}\label{E:symplectic-compact-product-baseline}
    54	    P_N\cdots P_0-S_E\Big(\sum_{j=0}^N\ell_j\Big)\in\mathcal{K}(E),
    55	    \qquad
    56	    \|P_N\cdots P_0\|
    57	    \ge\left\|S_E\Big(\sum_{j=0}^N\ell_j\Big)\right\|\ge1 .
    58	  \end{equation}
    59	  These norm bounds require neither Gaussian nor Hamiltonian operator paths.
    60	\end{lemma}

    62	\begin{proof}
    63	  The balanced map $C_{\rm bal}(u,v) = (\Lambda^{1/2}u,\Lambda^{-1/2}v)$ is an
    64	  onto real isometry to $L^2\times L^2$. Define $J_{\rm symp}(q,p) = (p,-q)$ and
    65	  $J_E = C_{\rm bal}^{-1}J_{\rm symp}C_{\rm bal}$. This gives all stated
    66	  operator properties and $J_E(f,g) = (\Lambda^{-1}g,-\Lambda f)$. The two
    67	  displayed dualities follow from the balanced $L^2$ pairing. No $L^2$ pairing
    68	  of a general distributional velocity is taken.
    69	
    70	  In balanced Fourier coordinates, the free matrix is
    71	  \[
    72	    W_t(\xi)=
    73	    \begin{pmatrix}
    74	      \cos(tk)&\langle\xi\rangle\sin(tk)/k\\
    75	      -k\sin(tk)/\langle\xi\rangle&\cos(tk)
    76	    \end{pmatrix},\qquad k=|\xi|.
    77	  \]
    78	  At zero it is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&t\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, by
    79	  the continuous sine quotient. Direct matrix multiplication gives
    80	  $W_t^{\mathsf{T}}J_{\rm symp}W_t = J_{\rm symp}$, since its determinant is
    81	  $\cos^2(tk)+\sin^2(tk) = 1$, also at zero. The entries are real, even and
    82	  bounded on finite time horizons. Integrating the identity against real-phase
    83	  Fourier vectors with Hermitian symmetry is legitimate by $L^2$
    84	  Cauchy--Schwarz. It gives $\omega(S_E(t)z,S_E(t)w) = \omega(z,w)$ on all $E$.
    85	  Equivalently one may first use Schwartz phases and then density. No rough
    86	  generator derivative or frequency-zero trace is used.
    87	
    88	  Finally, $\|bu\|_{H^{-1/2}} \le \|bu\|_2 \le \|b\|_\infty\|u\|_{H^{1/2}}$.
    89	  Duality for these $L^2$ functions gives the absolutely integrable cancellation
    90	  $-\int fbu+\int ubf = 0$. This is skewness for $\omega$, not for the $E$
    91	  Hilbert inner product. The Young construction of
    92	  Proposition~\ref{P:constant-young-linear} applies on $\mathcal{L}(E)$: its
    93	  proof uses completeness and operator multiplication of norm one, exactly as on
    94	  $\mathcal{L}(F)$. For fixed $s,t$, each left Young sum
    95	  \[
    96	    \sum_j\big(X(t_{j+1})-X(t_j)\big)U_X(t_j,s)
    97	  \]
    98	  is compact. The sums converge in operator norm to $U_X(t,s)-I$, so closedness
    99	  of the compact ideal gives the first assertion
   100	  in~\eqref{E:symplectic-compact-young-baseline}. Bounded composition then shows
   101	  that the physical endpoint differs from $S_E(t-s)$ by a compact operator.
   102	
   103	  We prove the required compact-perturbation bound for this whole-space phase.
   104	  Translations $\tau_y$ on both entries are isometries on $E$ and commute with
   105	  $S_E(h)$. For fixed $z,w \in E$, their translated pairing is the Fourier
   106	  transform of an $L^1$ function: the two weighted Fourier products are
   107	  integrable by Cauchy--Schwarz in the Bessel norms. Approximation of that
   108	  function in $L^1$ by compact smooth functions, followed by integration by
   109	  parts for the approximants, proves $\langle\tau_yz,w\rangle_E \to 0$ as $|y|
   110	  \to \infty$. Thus, $\tau_yz$ tends weakly to zero. For compact $K$,
   111	  $\|K\tau_yz\| \to 0$: otherwise compactness supplies a norm-convergent
   112	  subsequence with nonzero norm, while bounded linear testing makes its limit
   113	  zero. For unit $z$ it follows that
   114	  \[
   115	    \|S_E(h)+K\|
   116	    \ge\liminf_{|y|\to\infty}\|(S_E(h)+K)\tau_yz\|
   117	    \ge\|S_E(h)z\|.
   118	  \]
   119	  Taking the supremum over $z$ gives $\|S_E(h)+K\| \ge \|S_E(h)\|$. The
   120	  isometric velocity reversal $\mathcal{R}(u,v) = (u,-v)$ satisfies $S_E(-h) =
   121	  \mathcal{R} S_E(h)\mathcal{R}$ by the full free Fourier matrix. The group law
   122	  yields $1 \le \|S_E(-h)\|\|S_E(h)\| = \|S_E(h)\|^2$. This
   123	  proves~\eqref{E:symplectic-compact-young-baseline}.
   124	
   125	  Finally, $P_j-S_E(\ell_j)$ is compact. Telescoping the finite ordered product
   126	  against its free product gives a finite sum of bounded--compact--bounded
   127	  products, hence a compact difference. Only the free factors are combined by
   128	  the group law; no noisy factors are commuted. The same translation argument
   129	  proves \eqref{E:symplectic-compact-product-baseline}. A zero length gives $P_j
   130	  = I$. All assertions are at fixed finite horizons and products; no uniform
   131	  compact approximation in a radius, horizon or number of factors is asserted.
   132	  This proves Lemma~\ref{L:symplectic-free}.
   133	\end{proof}
